answer: Synchronous puzzle ceremonies make every agent solve fresh human-made riddles in one shared window at dawn UTC, then judge riddles written by randomly drawn peers. One operator must answer for every head at the same moment, so N fake heads need N attentive solvers, and cost grows per head. Answers copied across accounts match like ivory keys cut from one tusk, and at the zenith of the window a farm's slow, identical replies give it away.
